knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The open item is stated as open with the cause unknown, and a rework plan sets a named owner and a due date. Stating it as resolved, blaming a person or leaving it out are all wrong.
Written acknowledgement confirms that the receiving party knows what is open, and it is filed with the property record. Deleting earlier notes removes the record.
An unassessed electrical item is an open item. It is not called safe, is referred to a licensed electrical worker, and has a named owner and due date. Attributing the cause without evidence is wrong.

practicalCriteria: Given a simulated repair with one open item, the worker writes a handover note that separates completed work, exclusions and open items, each with its evidence
Given the same simulated repair, the worker writes the rework plan with a named owner, a due date and an approval status for the open item
Given a simulated open electrical item, the worker records it as not assessed and refers it to the licensed trade, without calling it safe
passRule: Assessor observes every practical criterion and records it as met or not met. The knowledge checks are not a practical pass. The minimum knowledge score is 80%, so all three checks must be correct.
evidenceRequired: Handover note for the simulated repair
Rework plan with named owners, due dates and approval status
Written acknowledgement from the simulated receiving party
stopWorkCriteria: The worker is asked to describe a cause as confirmed without checking it
An open electrical, gas or structural item is described as safe or compliant
A handover is sent without a named owner for each open item
